projectDescription: A low-cost, mobile-first rental discovery website for Bengaluru/Bangalore with locality and listing browsing, listing details, and direct WhatsApp or phone contact. Launch with manual moderation and staged Google Forms/Sheets submissions.

questions.question: Which language should the website use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing and a build step.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Keeps a small static MVP simple to host and maintain.

questions.rationale: A plain static MVP benefits from the smallest possible toolchain and can deploy directly to GitHub Pages or Netlify.

questions.question: Which frontend approach should power the MVP?

options.label: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
options.description: Lowest hosting and maintenance cost for a discovery-first static site.

options.label: React
options.description: Component-based UI with a client build pipeline.

options.label: Vue
options.description: Component-based UI with a lightweight build pipeline.

questions.rationale: The first release needs browsing and contact links, not a complex application runtime.

questions.question: Confirm the frontend MVP features and any essential change.
questions.recommendedChoice: Homepage; locality browsing; listing browsing and filters; listing detail; direct WhatsApp/phone contact; submission and moderation entry points; responsive mobile-first layout.
questions.answer: Homepage; locality browsing; listing browsing and filters; listing detail; direct WhatsApp/phone contact; submission and moderation entry points; responsive mobile-first layout.
questions.rationale: These features match the requested discovery-first launch while keeping communication outside the product.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores are needed for the MVP?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use static listing data initially and link submissions to Google Forms/Sheets.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store uploaded listing images or other media in a managed object store.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Use a relational database for listings, users, and moderation workflows.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The launch is intentionally static; Google Forms/Sheets remain an external intake tool, with a later data-backed stage planned separately.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in to access application API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require sign-in for application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: Keep browsing and direct contact links public; moderate submissions manually.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The MVP has no in-app messaging, accounts, or private user workflow.
